note: typed_entity_example is a reference implementation of the Typed Entity pattern. It registers two repositories: node.article (default wrapper Drupal\typed_entity_example\WrappedEntities\Article, variant BakingArticle, renderer Full) and the bundle-less user (wrapper User). Article implements domain logic (owner() returns a wrapped User, access() forbids on an inappropriate author nickname), ArticleRepository implements AccessibleInterface (forbid when >8 published articles), User::nickname() = email local-part, Full renderer sets a cyan background in preprocess(). It has no config/permissions/plugin types of its own. Medium cases enable the submodule and read the live repository registry/definitions; hard cases create a real article/user and verify the module wraps them into the correct example wrapped-entity class. cleanup uninstalls the submodule (baseline: disabled).

evals.prompt: Which entity types (and bundle) does the Drupal typed_entity_example submodule provide typed repositories for?
evals.expected_output: It provides ArticleRepository for node / bundle article, and UserRepository for the bundle-less user entity.

evals.prompt: In typed_entity_example, the article repository has a default wrapped-entity class and a specialized variant. Name both wrapper classes and say which is the variant.
evals.expected_output: The default (fallback) wrapper is Article; the variant is BakingArticle (declared via new ClassWithVariants(Article::class, [BakingArticle::class])).

evals.prompt: The example ArticleRepository implements AccessibleInterface to demonstrate repository-level access control. Under what condition does its access() method forbid access?
evals.expected_output: ArticleRepository::access() returns AccessResult::forbidden() when more than eight published articles exist (it counts published nodes of the article bundle); otherwise it is neutral.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, the typed_entity_example submodule registers a typed repository for a bundle-less entity type. Inspect the live repositories and name that entity type.
evals.expected_output: The bundle-less repository is for the user entity (repository id 'user', wrapper User). Discover via \Drupal::service(Drupal\typed_entity\RepositoryManager::class)->getAll() and read each repository's getEntityType()->id() / getBundle() (the one with a NULL bundle is user).

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, inspect the typed_entity_example repository for the article content type and give the class name of its default (fallback) wrapped-entity class.
evals.expected_output: The node.article repository's fallback wrapper is Drupal\typed_entity_example\WrappedEntities\Article. Read it from the plugin definition: \Drupal::service('plugin.manager.typed_entity_repository')->getDefinition('node.article')['wrappers']->getFallback().

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (with typed_entity_example enabled), create and save a new Article node with the title 'TEE Article Probe'. The goal is that the Typed Entity system wraps this node into the example module's Article wrapped-entity class. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an article node titled 'TEE Article Probe' (e.g. via the article repository's createEntity(['title' => 'TEE Article Probe']) then ->getEntity()->save(), or a plain Node::create). Because typed_entity_example registers the node.article repository, RepositoryManager::wrap() on it returns a Drupal\typed_entity_example\WrappedEntities\Article.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (with typed_entity_example enabled), create and save a new active user account with the email 'tee_probe_user@example.com'. The goal is that the Typed Entity system wraps this user into the example module's User wrapped-entity class. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create the user (e.g. the user repository's createEntity(['name' => 'tee_probe_user', 'mail' => 'tee_probe_user@example.com', 'status' => 1]) then ->getEntity()->save(), or User::create). Because typed_entity_example registers the bundle-less user repository, RepositoryManager::wrap() on the account returns a Drupal\typed_entity_example\WrappedEntities\User. (This site's email_registration module forces the username to equal the email, so the email is the identifier.)
